title: Wholesale and Retail Buyers, Except Farm Products

tasks.short: Analyze sales, market signals and stock to anticipate demand and inventory needs.

steps.what: Retrieve sales, stock, returns and outstanding orders from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Read category reports and economic releases held in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved category reports and economic releases.
loop.output: Dated market signals with source passages and affected categories.
loop.check: Require source passages and dates; buyer checks material signals and conflicting interpretations.
loop.stop: At most 20 documents and two extraction passes per run; unreadable sources go to buyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sources express demand drivers in varied prose; fixed fields cannot capture them reliably.

steps.what: Combine extracts and calculate trends, stock cover and baseline demand in {SPREADSHEET}.
Adjust demand assumptions for promotions, stockouts and market signals in {SPREADSHEET}.
Agree inventory assumptions and the forecast with the buyer and sales manager.
Record the approved forecast and inventory targets in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled feeds from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}; deterministic calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feed a {BI} view of demand, stock cover and forecast error. A bounded loop extracts source-linked market signals from {DOCS}, while buyers adjust assumptions and managers approve forecasts. The approved version updates inventory targets in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product identifiers, promotion calendars and stockout history often needed manual alignment. Report interpretation and category judgement remained separate from planning systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and statistical methods handle structured inputs. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building joins, scenario controls and validation; bounded extraction helps with prose.
tasks.still_hard: Lost sales during stockouts, new products and changing promotions weaken historical forecasts. Backtesting cannot establish demand for an unseen assortment.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer distinguishes temporary noise from a real category shift and accepts commercial risk under uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: The buyer spends more time comparing scenarios and investigating forecast misses. Within delegated limits, they can propose weekly inventory reallocations; spending authority requires a separate delegation.

reach.task: Compare inventory allocations across categories.
reach.learn: Working-capital constraints, forecast bias and portfolio trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Structured sales and inventory analysis can use deterministic pipelines, statistical forecasts and dashboards.
Source-linked extraction can assist market reading, but category interpretation still needs review.

assumptions: This describes a buyer with system records and a spreadsheet planning bridge in a mid-size European company.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates for one category pilot, not measured results.
Available connectors support scheduled extracts; custom historical alignment still needs code.
Analysis uses category aggregates. GDPR applies if personal data enters the inputs; EU AI Act duties depend on intended use.
Access estimates include national employee consultation requirements if the implementation changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which planning features and connectors are already licensed?
Are product identifiers, promotions and stockout histories reliable?
Who approves forecasts, and which inventory decisions are delegated?
What are current forecast error, preparation time and reporting frequency?
research_questions: Which baseline forecast beats current practice in historical backtests?
Do extracted market signals improve decisions beyond sales and promotion data?
new_work: Review extracted market signals and conflicting sources.
Resolve missing products, stale feeds and promotion mismatches.
Monitor forecast bias and document overrides.
Maintain calculations, source permissions and connector mappings.
tasks.statement: Monitor and analyze sales records, trends, or economic conditions to anticipate consumer buying patterns, company sales, and needed inventory.

tasks.short: Check merchandise invoices and approve payment or returns under agreed terms.

steps.what: Register the supplier invoice and route it to the responsible buyer.
Retrieve the purchase order, goods receipt and relevant contract terms.
Compare invoiced prices and quantities with orders, receipts and agreed allowances.
Resolve price, receipt or quality discrepancies with suppliers and warehouse staff.
Approve invoice payment or merchandise return within delegated authority.
Record payment authorization and notify the finance team.
Send the approved return request and instructions to the supplier and warehouse.

tasks.design: Configured matching in the {ERP} checks invoices against {PROCUREMENT} orders and {OPS_SYSTEM} receipts, with a linked evidence pack from {DOCS}. A configured approval flow presents exceptions to the buyer, records payment or return authorization and sends approved notices through {EMAIL}. Finance retains its separate payment-release control, and approval changes invalidate pending notices.
tasks.previous_blocker: Matching features often cover clean invoices, but missing receipts and scattered quality evidence force manual investigation. Payment and return authority also need explicit separation from data preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching and approval configuration can handle routine cases. Faster connector development can bring receipt and quality evidence into the same view without adding a model.
tasks.still_hard: Partial deliveries, rebates, damaged goods and disputed acceptance require judgement. Supplier credits and physical returns may remain unresolved after the initial authorization.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer decides whether a discrepancy warrants payment, a negotiated adjustment or a return while protecting the supplier relationship.

ambition.what: A weekly supplier discrepancy review that identifies recurring shortages and invoice errors.

tasks.altitude: The buyer reviews evidence-backed exceptions and recurring supplier problems instead of retrieving routine records. Payment-release rights remain with finance; no new financial authority is assumed.

reach.task: Track return requests through receipt of supplier credits.
reach.learn: Credit-note matching, return identifiers and unresolved-balance reporting.

reach.task: Recommend corrective action for suppliers with recurring discrepancies.
reach.learn: Supplier performance measures, dispute patterns and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Invoice-to-order-to-receipt matching and approval routing are established finance-system capabilities.
Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates; this supports rate-checking capability, not merchandise-return decisions.
Pactum's documented SUEZ case concerns requisition review, so its reported savings are not an invoice-authorization forecast.

assumptions: Step shares describe effort across a mixed queue; payment and return notices are alternative branches.
Remaining time estimates exclude later bank release, physical shipping and credit settlement.
Existing invoice intake supports structured invoices or validated document capture; unsupported files enter an exception queue.
The judgement prior fits disputes, but routine matching and routing have greater rule coverage.
Supplier bank details cannot be changed through this workflow.
GDPR applies to personal data in invoices and contacts. EU AI Act obligations depend on actual AI use; this proposed flow is deterministic.
Access estimates include national consultation review where required, without assuming employee monitoring.
unknowns: Invoice formats and existing intake, matching and approval capabilities.
Customer matching tolerances, rebate treatment and partial-delivery rules.
Who can authorize payment, returns and supplier credits.
Receipt completeness and availability of quality evidence.
Separation of buyer authorization from finance payment release.
Applicable access and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which standard interfaces expose partial receipts and credit-note links consistently?
Which matching configurations support quantity discrepancies without concealing unresolved quality disputes?
new_work: Handle failed matches and missing receipts.
Maintain tolerances, approval limits and routing.
Review recurring discrepancy reports.
Monitor duplicate invoices, connector failures and unresolved supplier credits.
tasks.statement: Authorize payment of invoices or return of merchandise.

tasks.short: Agree buying priorities and budgets with store or merchandise managers.

steps.what: Gather store sales, stock, commitments and remaining buying budget.
Read managers' requests and collect local demand concerns.

loop.input: Selected store requests and customer feedback, with the store buying summary.
loop.output: Source-linked requests grouped by product, store, urgency and unresolved question.
loop.check: Preserve each request and its source; flag conflicting requests; buyer checks priorities and omissions.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair attempt; ambiguous requests stay open for discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Managers express local needs in free text; structured request forms use deterministic grouping.

steps.what: Prepare buying options showing margin, stock coverage and budget effects.
Discuss local demand, operational constraints and competing buying priorities.
Agree budget allocations and which purchases should proceed.
Record agreed priorities, update buying plans and assign follow-up actions.

tasks.design: A shared {BI} view combines {ERP} budgets and sales with {OPS_SYSTEM} stock and {PROCUREMENT} commitments. A bounded loop groups selected requests from {EMAIL} and {CHAT}, while deterministic scenarios show the consequences of each option. Managers agree allocations in conversation, then configured {WORKFLOW} updates {PROJECT} actions and the buying plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Store context arrives separately from financial and stock data. Spreadsheet scenarios take preparation, while final priorities depend on local knowledge and competing goals.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared datasets and reusable scenario calculations can remove repeated preparation. Bounded classification can organize free-text requests without deciding which store should receive budget.
tasks.still_hard: Local demand signals may conflict with historical sales. Managers must negotiate scarce stock, budget and operational capacity, and forecasts remain uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer draws out local knowledge and builds agreement on trade-offs that store-level numbers cannot resolve.

ambition.what: A monthly store-specific buying review for small stores without a dedicated merchandise planner.

tasks.altitude: The buyer enters discussions with current scenarios and spends more time testing managers' assumptions. Budget approval stays with the merchandise manager; the buyer gains capacity to prepare store-specific proposals.

reach.task: Prepare cross-store allocation recommendations.
reach.learn: Budget governance, scenario analysis and facilitation of competing priorities.

reach.task: Check supplier feasibility for proposed store buying plans.
reach.learn: Minimum-order quantities, lead-time constraints and consolidated ordering.

evidence.claim: Budget, stock coverage and margin scenarios can be calculated deterministically from governed records.
A bounded classification loop can organize requests while leaving prioritization and budget agreement to people.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are estimates; meeting duration varies with the decision.
Conversation remains the largest single step, consistent with the communication prior.
Preparation is visible despite the low-drudgery prior; email is one source of requests, not the whole consultation.
Approved priorities can be captured in structured fields, so follow-up does not require automatic meeting transcription.
The solution reuses sales, stock and order connectors from the buying task where possible.
GDPR applies to personal data in messages. EU AI Act applicability depends on intended use; this design does not score employees.
National rules determine whether employee consultation is required; access ranges include that review where applicable.
unknowns: Who owns store budgets and approves cross-store reallocations.
Frequency and format of store requests and consultation meetings.
Availability of store-level sales, stock and committed-budget records.
Which small stores lack merchandise planning support.
Permissions for selected messages and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which stock-coverage measures work reliably with intermittent store demand?
Which scenario formats help managers compare margin, availability and budget consequences?
new_work: Review request grouping and omitted local context.
Maintain scenario assumptions and budget definitions.
Resolve stale records and inconsistent store identifiers.
Track whether agreed buying actions improved availability and sell-through.
tasks.statement: Consult with store or merchandise managers about budgets or goods to be purchased.

tasks.short: Train sales or clerical staff and supervise their merchandise-related work.

steps.what: Review outstanding work, recurring errors and completed training.
Choose work assignments and coaching priorities for each staff member.
Prepare examples and exercises from approved procedures and merchandise information.

loop.input: Approved procedures, product facts and a buyer-selected coaching topic
loop.check: Validate source references and required fields; buyer checks accuracy before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per topic; missing sources return the existing approved material.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed templates cannot adapt explanations and examples to varied coaching topics.

steps.what: Demonstrate the work, answer questions and coach staff through practice.
Check completed work and decide whether further coaching or correction is needed.
Record completed coaching and schedule agreed follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Configure a work and training summary using {PROCUREMENT}, {PROJECT} and {LMS}, without worker scoring. A bounded drafting loop prepares source-linked exercises from {DOCS} for buyer approval, while {WORKFLOW} records human-confirmed completion and schedules follow-ups.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coaching materials need frequent updates, while preparation and completion records sit in separate places. The coaching conversation itself depends on trust and observation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning features can handle assignments and reminders. Bounded drafting can adapt approved content, and AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting records.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing understanding, workload fairness and confidence remains human. GDPR governs employee data; EU AI Act requirements depend on intended use, and national rules may require employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer notices confusion, gives tactful feedback and distinguishes a training gap from an unreasonable workload.

ambition.what: Short practice clinics for recurring merchandise-handling errors

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends less time preparing exercises and recording attendance, with more room for practice and feedback. Staffing and performance decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Resolve routine order-entry errors
reach.learn: Common validation failures, correction procedures and clear instructional examples

evidence.claim: Learning records, reminders and completion workflows can use existing configuration.
Source-grounded exercise drafting can support preparation, but does not establish coaching effectiveness.
Employment-related AI classification depends on intended use; simple training administration is different from worker evaluation.

assumptions: The buyer has delegated responsibility for a small sales or clerical team.
Approved procedures and basic training records exist.
The solution does not infer employee scores or make staffing decisions.
Build ranges cover one team; consultation timing is provisional.
unknowns: The buyer's actual supervisory authority
Whether training records and work queues can be accessed together
Employee-data retention and access restrictions
Applicable national rules, employee representation and consultation lead times
research_questions: Which learning and reminder features can be configured without new code?
Can useful exercises be produced without personal employee information?
Does the final intended use trigger additional employment-related AI requirements?
new_work: Approve exercises and remove unsupported instructions.
Keep source procedures current.
Correct completion records and failed reminders.
Maintain access controls and agreed employee-data retention.
tasks.statement: Train or supervise sales or clerical staff.

tasks.short: Give clerks accurate, approved merchandise data for price tags.

steps.what: Retrieve approved prices, product identifiers and season codes from the {ERP}.
Copy tag fields and calculate displayed price changes in {SPREADSHEET}.
Check tag fields, arithmetic and effective dates in {SPREADSHEET}.
Send validated tag data and instructions to the procurement clerk through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to expose approved tag fields and validate prices, identifiers and effective dates. A deterministic adapter sends versioned tag instructions directly to the label-printing system in {OTHER}, replacing the {SPREADSHEET} and routine {EMAIL} handoff. Invalid records enter an exception queue in {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product and price records were disconnected from the printing process. A spreadsheet and mailbox provided a cheap bridge.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and validation features can supply approved data. AI-assisted coding makes a small field-mapping adapter cheaper to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect master data, overlapping price changes and unsupported printer formats still need correction. Consumer price-display requirements vary under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer resolves ambiguous price instructions and decides whether an unusual promotion needs a different presentation.
tasks.altitude: Routine tag preparation disappears where the manual bridge exists. The buyer handles exceptions and gains no additional pricing authority.

reach.task: Resolve rejected label batches and control reprints.
reach.learn: Template fields, effective dates and label version checks.

evidence.claim: Approved structured product and price data can feed label instructions through deterministic mappings and validation.
Benefits may be small where the existing price-to-label connection already works.

assumptions: The task communicates already approved prices; setting prices is outside its scope.
The example company still uses a manual spreadsheet and email bridge.
Configured validation replaces the worksheet check using authoritative source fields.
Invalid records are held rather than corrected or released automatically.
Ranges cover one label format and one receiving system.
Access work includes any consultation required by national rules; no employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Is tag data already linked directly to label printing?
Can the receiving system import structured batches?
Which fields, price-display rules and effective-date conventions apply?
How much buyer time does this handoff currently consume?
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove the manual bridge without an adapter?
Which validation rules prevent the actual label errors seen today?
new_work: Correct rejected master data and conflicting price dates.
Maintain field mappings and label templates.
Monitor failed batches and prevent duplicate releases.
Approve changes to price-display rules through the existing pricing process.
tasks.statement: Provide clerks with information to print on price tags, such as price, mark-ups or mark-downs, manufacturer number, season code, or style number.

tasks.short: Choose merchandise, channels and timing for advertising.

steps.what: Compile sales, margins, stock and previous promotion results.
Check campaign budget, supplier funding, availability and advertising deadlines.
Select candidate products and assess customer appeal, margin and stock risk.
Agree proposed products, advertising channels and timing with marketing.
Prepare the campaign brief with products, prices, channels and dates.
Approve the campaign brief and release it to campaign execution.

tasks.design: Join {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ADS} data into a promotion view in {BI}, with budget and availability checks. Generate a campaign brief in {DOCS} from the buyer's selections and route approval through {WORKFLOW} before handing it to marketing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales, stock and campaign results use different identifiers and reporting periods. Choosing an attractive offer also needs commercial judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, calculations and brief templates. Existing reporting and approval features can handle much of the flow.
tasks.still_hard: Promotion uplift is uncertain. Stock changes, supplier commitments and channel effects can invalidate an otherwise sound plan.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer understands customer appeal, category positioning and when a low-margin promotion earns its place.

ambition.what: Weekly stock-aware revisions to the promotion shortlist

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends less time reconciling reports and more time testing campaign choices. They can propose weekly revisions; budget and publication rights remain with the existing approvers.

reach.task: Balance promotional commitments against category budgets
reach.learn: Category contribution, supplier funding and portfolio trade-offs

evidence.claim: Structured sales, stock and margin data support deterministic comparisons and campaign brief generation.
Commercial selection and channel trade-offs remain judgement work; build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The company runs planned merchandise promotions with buyer and marketing input.
The campaign constraints already exist as structured fields or maintained records.
Step shares describe combined task effort, not measured time.
The build covers one category and existing campaign channels.
unknowns: Whether product identifiers match across the source systems
Who can approve promotional prices, budgets and campaign release
Whether stock reservations and supplier funding are recorded reliably
Which access permissions and national consultation requirements apply
research_questions: Which promotion and approval features are already licensed?
Can historical data distinguish promotion effects from seasonality and stock shortages?
new_work: Resolve missing identifiers and stale stock feeds.
Maintain margin, availability and supplier-funding checks.
Compare proposed promotion outcomes with actual results.
Review campaign briefs at the release gate.
tasks.statement: Determine which products should be featured in advertising, the advertising medium to be used, or when the ads should be run.

tasks.short: Track competitors' advertised merchandise, prices and promotional activity.

steps.what: Collect competitors' advertisements from publications, websites and promotional messages.
Record advertised products, prices, dates and offer conditions.

loop.input: Archived advertisement text and images with source and collection date
loop.output: Product, pack size, advertised price, validity dates and offer conditions
loop.check: Validate currencies, dates and price formats; require source locations; review ambiguous or incomplete records.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per advertisement; unresolved fields enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Advertisement layouts and promotional wording vary; use deterministic parsing where structured feeds exist.

steps.what: Compare comparable products, unit prices and changes against previous offers.
Assess which advertised changes matter for the category.
Share relevant observations and flag possible buying or promotion responses.

tasks.design: Collect permitted public advertisements from the web-publication category of {OTHER} and subscribed messages in {EMAIL}, retaining dated originals in {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop populates offer records in {DATA_PLATFORM}; deterministic comparisons feed {BI}, and {WORKFLOW} distributes buyer-confirmed observations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advertisements mix images, changing layouts and conditional prices. Manual collection and inconsistent product matching make comparisons expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded text-and-image extraction can handle varied layouts. AI-assisted coding reduces connector and validation effort, while unit-price calculations remain deterministic.
tasks.still_hard: Advertisements show advertised offers, not realised sales. Access restrictions, incomplete coverage, loyalty conditions and near-equivalent products limit comparisons.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer distinguishes a meaningful competitive move from an isolated offer and understands whether a response fits the category.
tasks.altitude: The buyer reviews exceptions and commercial implications instead of collecting clippings. They can raise response proposals sooner; pricing and purchasing authority stays with existing roles.

reach.task: Decide category responses to competitive promotions
reach.learn: Comparable-product selection, margin consequences and limits of advertised-price evidence

evidence.claim: Public advertisement monitoring can combine scheduled collection, bounded extraction and deterministic comparisons.
Product equivalence and offer conditions require checks before unit-price comparisons are treated as comparable.
The digest provides no documented competitor-monitoring case; build ranges and remaining effort are estimates.

assumptions: OTHER denotes public websites and digital publication archives.
The first release covers a fixed competitor watchlist and one merchandise category.
Sources permit the proposed collection; inaccessible sources require supplied files.
Human gates cover extracted records and new product matches before decision-facing publication.
Established product matches and validated calculations can run without repeated approval.
unknowns: Which competitors, publications and regions need coverage
Source access rights, licensing terms and collection limits
Whether comparable-product mappings already exist
The required freshness and acceptable gaps in coverage
Whether collected material contains personal data requiring GDPR controls
research_questions: Which sources provide structured feeds or permitted downloads?
How often do conditional offers prevent valid unit-price comparison?
What extraction and matching error rate is acceptable before publication?
new_work: Review ambiguous prices, dates, conditions and product matches.
Maintain source connectors and permitted collection schedules.
Detect missing sources and changed advertisement layouts.
Refresh product mappings and suppress duplicate alerts.
Track whether reported observations lead to useful commercial decisions.
tasks.statement: Monitor competitors' sales activities by following their advertisements in newspapers or other media.

tasks.short: Compare environmental evidence for competing merchandise and recommend buying trade-offs.

steps.what: Request missing environmental evidence from suppliers through {EMAIL}.
Read supplier declarations, certificates and environmental studies stored in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Supplier declarations, certificates, studies and the environmental criteria.
loop.output: Draft evidence register with values, units, scope, dates, source passages and missing information.
loop.check: Require source references; validate field types and units; buyer checks scope and material claims. Extraction does not establish authenticity.
loop.stop: At most ten documents per product and two passes; missing or conflicting evidence goes to buyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence mixes tables and prose with inconsistent descriptions of scope, exclusions and product coverage.

steps.what: Compare compatible metrics and record evidence gaps in {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss conflicting evidence and environmental trade-offs with the buyer.
Record the environmental recommendation and accepted trade-offs in {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: Configure evidence requests and expiry reminders in {WORKFLOW}, with supplier documents held in {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts an evidence register; deterministic comparisons on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feed {BI}, converting only compatible metrics and exposing missing scope. The buyer reviews comparability, consults a specialist and records the approved recommendation in {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Environmental evidence uses inconsistent scopes, units and product coverage. Cheap document storage did not make claims comparable or trustworthy.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake and deterministic unit checks already work. Bounded extraction reduces document reading effort, while AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of maintaining an evidence register.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity, lifecycle boundaries and trade-offs between impacts require expertise. Missing evidence cannot safely become an average score or a claim of environmental superiority.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer challenges supplier claims and weighs environmental uncertainty against durability, affordability and commercial suitability.

ambition.what: Pre-buy environmental evidence clinic for assistant buyers

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends less time finding certificates and more time challenging weak comparisons. They can give assistant buyers documented advice; authority to waive environmental requirements needs explicit delegation.

reach.task: Set category environmental evidence requirements.
reach.learn: Lifecycle boundaries, evidence strength and the consequences of exclusion thresholds.

reach.task: Request comparable environmental evidence during supplier qualification.
reach.learn: Functional units, certificate coverage and evidence expiry.

evidence.claim: Document extraction can structure environmental evidence, but does not establish authenticity or lifecycle comparability.
Deterministic comparisons can convert compatible units and flag missing scope without resolving environmental trade-offs.

assumptions: A sustainability specialist is available for disputed or material comparisons.
Routine evidence requests use approved wording, known supplier contacts and bounded reminders.
Compared metrics remain separate unless an approved method establishes comparability and weighting.
The structured-input prior fits numeric comparisons; underlying evidence still commonly includes declarations and certificates.
Ranges cover one category and an agreed evidence schema, excluding commissioned environmental studies.
GDPR applies to supplier contact data; EU AI Act obligations depend on the intended use.
Access estimates include consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which environmental criteria and exclusion thresholds are approved?
Which evidence sources can be accessed and reused?
Who verifies certificate authenticity and resolves disputed claims?
Is specialist support internal or external?
Which national product and environmental-claim requirements affect the merchandise?
research_questions: Which metrics are genuinely comparable within the selected category?
Can suppliers provide structured evidence instead of repeated document requests?
Which extraction errors could change a buying recommendation?
new_work: Review extracted scope, units and product coverage.
Verify material certificates and investigate conflicting claims.
Maintain evidence criteria, expiry rules and comparison methods.
Handle unanswered requests and supplier corrections.
Record unresolved uncertainty alongside recommendations.
tasks.statement: Analyze environmental aspects of competing merchandise when making buying decisions.

tasks.short: Choose merchandise, agree buying quantities and place orders within approved budgets.

steps.what: Review sales, stock, outstanding orders and available buying budget.
Compare supplier quotes, delivery dates, minimum quantities and commercial terms.

loop.input: Supplier quotes and contract passages for the shortlisted merchandise.
loop.output: Source-linked prices, units, minimum quantities, lead times and terms.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units and arithmetic; flag missing terms; buyer checks consequential fields against sources.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per quote; unresolved fields return to the buyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express terms in inconsistent tables and free text; calculations remain deterministic.

steps.what: Choose products, suppliers and quantities against margin, demand and assortment priorities.
Create a purchase order from the buying decision and agreed supplier terms.
Approve the purchase commitment under delegated spending limits.
Send the approved purchase order to the supplier.
Record the supplier confirmation and resolve changed quantities or dates.

loop.input: Supplier confirmation and the issued purchase order.
loop.output: Proposed confirmation fields and differences from the order.
loop.check: Match supplier and order identifiers; compare quantities, dates and prices; buyer approves changes.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; ambiguous confirmations enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Email confirmations contain free text; structured portal confirmations use direct field mapping.

tasks.design: A reusable dashboard on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines {ERP} sales, {OPS_SYSTEM} stock and {PROCUREMENT} commitments into buying scenarios. Bounded extraction turns documents in {DOCS} and confirmations in {EMAIL} into checked fields; configured {PROCUREMENT} flows create and issue orders after recorded approval. Changes to an approved order invalidate its approval before another external commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales, stock and supplier terms sit in different places. Assortment choices depend on commercial judgement, while connecting the supporting records required bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval features and accessible exports can handle much of the process. AI-assisted coding reduces connector and scenario-tool development effort; bounded extraction handles variable documents.
tasks.still_hard: New-product demand, substitutes, supplier reliability and changing tastes remain uncertain. Incorrect units or stale stock can make a plausible buying scenario wrong.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer balances customer appeal, downside risk and supplier trust when historical sales do not settle the choice.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly assortment reallocation between fast-selling and slow-selling merchandise.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling comparisons to reviewing assortment risks and testing smaller buying commitments. Spending authority remains unchanged; a wider trial budget needs explicit delegation.

reach.task: Recommend category budget reallocations.
reach.learn: Open-to-buy planning, working-capital exposure and portfolio margin.

reach.task: Improve order confirmation exception handling.
reach.learn: Item identifiers, unit conversions and purchase-order amendment controls.

evidence.claim: Sales, stock, budget and order comparisons can use deterministic calculations and dashboards.
Pactum supports procurement policy checks and negotiation within Coupa; this demonstrates adjacent procurement capability.
The vendor-reported SUEZ case describes reduced requisition review work; it does not establish retail buying savings.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Structured sales and stock support the input prior; judgement remains central to product selection.
The mailbox share reflects order issuance and confirmations, not every supplier interaction.
Existing approval configuration is reused where available; recorded approval covers issuance without a second approval.
Build ranges describe a limited category pilot and can share connectors with the other tasks.
GDPR applies to supplier contacts and EU AI Act applicability depends on intended use. National rules govern any employee consultation; the design does not require employee monitoring.
unknowns: Available connectors, export rights and item identifiers across the customer's systems.
Actual purchasing approval limits and who may amend an approved order.
Share of quotes and confirmations received as structured records.
Sales, stock and outstanding-order data quality and freshness.
Applicable national consultation requirements and employee representative arrangements.
research_questions: Which standard purchasing interfaces support order amendments and approval invalidation?
Which extraction checks best detect unit and currency mistakes in supplier quotes?
new_work: Review extracted commercial terms and changed confirmations.
Investigate stock, identifier and unit-conversion exceptions.
Maintain connectors, comparison rules and approval routing.
Compare buying scenarios with actual sell-through and margin.
tasks.statement: Buy merchandise or commodities for resale to wholesale or retail consumers.

tasks.short: Negotiate supplier prices, discounts and transport terms.

steps.what: Retrieve supplier contracts, purchase history and delivery performance.
Compare quoted prices, discount conditions and freight charges.

loop.input: Supplier quotations and contract clauses with source references.
loop.output: Structured prices, discount conditions, freight terms and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units and totals deterministically; buyer checks ambiguous clauses against sources.
loop.stop: At most two extraction attempts per document; leave unresolved fields blank for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structured quotations; varied prose and conditional clauses require bounded extraction.

steps.what: Prepare negotiation targets and cost scenarios within the buying mandate.
Discuss trade-offs and negotiate provisional terms with the supplier.
Approve negotiated terms against commercial limits and contract requirements.
Update purchasing records with approved prices, conditions and effective dates.

tasks.design: Connect {CLM}, {PROCUREMENT} and {ERP} to a reusable supplier comparison and cost calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop handles prose quotations, while templates generate negotiation briefs in {DOCS}. The buyer negotiates, the purchasing manager approves terms, and an integration updates {PROCUREMENT} from approved records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commercial terms arrive in varied documents, and supplier identifiers and effective dates differ across records. Bespoke comparisons and integrations were costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers implementation effort for connectors and calculators. Bounded extraction can turn varied quotations into reviewable fields without delegating bargaining.
tasks.still_hard: Rebates, freight liabilities and conditional discounts can hide material exceptions. Supplier leverage and relationship consequences remain difficult to encode.
tasks.human_edge: Read supplier intentions, exchange concessions and judge when a cheaper offer creates unacceptable dependency.

ambition.what: Compare consolidated versus split deliveries during weekly supplier negotiations.

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends less time assembling comparisons and more time testing concessions and delivery options. Commercial authority remains within the existing buying mandate.

reach.task: Maintain supplier prices and effective dates.
reach.learn: Learn supplier identifiers, unit conversions and how approved terms become purchasing records.

reach.task: Set negotiation limits for a merchandise category.
reach.learn: Learn working-capital trade-offs, supplier concentration and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Structured cost comparisons, approval routing and supplier-record updates can use deterministic software.
Pactum offers procurement policy checking and supplier negotiation capabilities; this supports feasibility, not equivalent bargaining outcomes.
The SUEZ vendor case documents requisition-review automation, not savings from this buyer negotiation workflow.

assumptions: Estimates cover one merchandise category with reusable exports or supported interfaces.
Negotiation conversations produce provisional terms until the required commercial approval.
Existing signing and purchasing controls continue to govern binding commitments.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the actual processing; national rules determine any employee consultation.
unknowns: Which supplier terms are structured and which exist only in documents?
Who can approve concessions and make binding supplier commitments?
Which interfaces and commercial-data access are available?
Does the proposed processing require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can existing quotation templates remove most extraction needs?
How reliably can conditional rebates be represented across the intended supplier document types?
new_work: Review ambiguous or unsupported extracted terms.
Maintain currencies, units, cost formulas and document mappings.
Resolve rejected record updates and conflicting effective dates.
Check that negotiation briefs use current contracts and approved mandates.
tasks.statement: Negotiate prices, discount terms, or transportation arrangements with suppliers.

tasks.short: Select suitable merchandise and place approved purchase orders.

steps.what: Check inventory targets, budget and merchandise requirements in the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}.
Compare supplier quotations, specifications and environmental evidence held in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Buying brief, supplier quotations, specifications and approved environmental recommendation.
loop.output: Source-linked quotation fields and explicit missing requirements.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units and required fields; deterministic code calculates totals; buyer checks material terms.
loop.stop: At most ten quotations and two passes per comparison; unresolved fields remain missing for buyer review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express specifications and exclusions in varied prose; calculations themselves remain deterministic.

steps.what: Inspect samples for quality, finish and suitability against merchandise requirements.
Select merchandise and quantities, recording the decision in {PROCUREMENT}.
Enter purchase order lines and agreed terms in {PROCUREMENT}.
Approve the purchase commitment against delegated limits in {PROCUREMENT}.
Send the approved purchase order to the supplier through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure {PROCUREMENT} to assemble buying briefs, create orders from approved selections and enforce spending approvals. A bounded loop extracts quotation terms from {DOCS}, while deterministic calculations compare quantities, costs and explicit requirements. Buyers inspect samples and select merchandise; only the approved order version is sent through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quotation formats differ, product records are incomplete and selected terms are often retyped. Physical quality and assortment judgement cannot be reduced to purchasing rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order and approval features handle the transaction. Bounded document extraction and faster connector development reduce the cost of preparing a reliable comparison.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier substitutions, ambiguous specifications and late term changes require investigation. Physical quality, consumer appeal and commercial commitments remain consequential judgements.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer judges whether merchandise will sell, recognises quality problems and balances margin against supplier reliability.

ambition.what: Structured quotation comparisons for small regional suppliers

tasks.altitude: The buyer can assess more regional suppliers without proportional paperwork. They gain capacity to recommend assortment changes; formal buying limits still depend on delegation.

reach.task: Assess category exposure to supplier failure.
reach.learn: Supplier concentration, contingency sourcing and approval thresholds.

reach.task: Maintain purchase order data quality.
reach.learn: Product identifiers, units, version control and duplicate prevention.

evidence.claim: Pactum checks requisitions against purchasing policy inside Coupa; this supports policy-check feasibility, not merchandise-selection accuracy.
The SUEZ vendor case reports reduced requisition review work; its results do not establish savings for retail assortment buying.
Quotation extraction, deterministic comparison and configured approval routing can assist buyers while preserving selection judgement.

assumptions: A procurement clerk prepares orders, with a purchasing manager approving commitments in this example.
Sample inspection applies to relevant new or changed merchandise, not every repeat order.
Build ranges cover one merchandise category and one order channel.
The existing {PROCUREMENT} supports approval routing and order transmission.
Supplier contact data is handled under GDPR; EU AI Act obligations are assessed for the actual use.
Access estimates include national employee consultation where process or monitoring changes require it.
unknowns: Which order preparation and transmission features are already configured?
Which buyers can commit spending without manager approval?
How many quotations require document extraction rather than structured import?
Which quality and environmental requirements are mandatory?
How often do selected terms change before order release?
research_questions: Which quotation fields cause the most ordering errors?
Can existing configuration create orders directly from approved selections?
new_work: Review extracted terms and unresolved specification differences.
Maintain product mappings and supplier master records.
Investigate blocked orders and failed transmissions.
Check that order amendments invalidate prior approval where required.
tasks.statement: Examine, select, order, or purchase merchandise consistent with quality, quantity, specification requirements, or other factors, such as environmental soundness.

tasks.short: Recommend merchandise prices, mark-ups and mark-downs.

steps.what: Retrieve sales, stock, purchase costs and current selling prices.
Calculate landed costs, current margins and stock ageing.
Compare mark-up and mark-down scenarios against margin and clearance targets.
Review commercial trade-offs and agree the pricing recommendation.
Send the agreed recommendation and supporting calculations to the pricing team.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations assemble {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ECOMMERCE} data on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic cost and pricing rules generate scenarios in {BI}, including margin floors and clearance constraints. After the sales manager approves a recommendation, {WORKFLOW} creates the pricing change request.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, stock and sales used different identifiers and refresh schedules. Scenario work depended on manually maintained formulas and undocumented commercial assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic calculations and approval flows are established capabilities. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of joining data and building a reviewable scenario interface.
tasks.still_hard: Sales changes do not reveal price sensitivity by themselves. Promotions, availability and competitor behaviour can make historical comparisons misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Judge customer price expectations, brand position and when clearing stock is worth sacrificing margin.

ambition.what: Make weekly ageing-stock mark-down recommendations instead of waiting for a clearance review.

tasks.altitude: The buyer reviews ranked exceptions and discusses commercial assumptions instead of rebuilding price workbooks. The role gains no automatic right to publish customer-facing prices.

reach.task: Balance category margin against stock exposure.
reach.learn: Learn contribution margins, inventory ageing and the limits of historical demand evidence.

reach.task: Maintain cost and price master data.
reach.learn: Learn effective dates, tax treatment, pack sizes and landed-cost reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Landed costs, margin floors and constrained price scenarios can be calculated without language models.
Reliable estimates of demand response require validation beyond comparing historical prices and sales.

assumptions: Estimates cover one category and a recommendation workflow, ending before price publication.
Initial scenarios use explicit rules and sensitivity ranges rather than an unvalidated demand model.
Pricing uses aggregated merchandise data without customer profiling.
Applicable national price-display and promotion rules are represented in the pricing policy; GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are checked for the actual design.
unknowns: Are freight, rebates, returns and taxes represented consistently in costs?
Who approves recommendations and who publishes prices?
Which margin floors, clearance targets and promotion restrictions apply?
Does existing {BI} or {WORKFLOW} configuration already cover the scenario and approval needs?
research_questions: Which simple pricing rules perform acceptably when backtested against past clearance periods?
What evidence would justify adding a demand-response model later?
new_work: Resolve stale costs, missing stock and mismatched product identifiers.
Maintain margin floors, rounding rules and promotion constraints.
Review scenario assumptions and unusual recommendations.
Compare realised outcomes with recommendations without attributing every sales change to price.
tasks.statement: Recommend mark-up rates, mark-down rates, or merchandise selling prices.

tasks.short: Learn customer needs and preferences through sales and purchasing colleagues.

steps.what: Review sales patterns and recorded customer requests before asking colleagues.
Ask sales and purchasing colleagues for recent needs and unmet demand.
Reply with customer examples, objections and requests missing from existing records.
Discuss examples, challenge assumptions and explore unmet customer needs.
Summarise needs, supporting examples, disagreements and evidence gaps.

loop.input: Written discussion notes, feedback responses and referenced customer signals.
loop.output: A needs brief linking themes to examples, with disagreements and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Require source references for each theme; buyer verifies meaning and removes unsupported generalisations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; unresolved contradictions remain explicit for human follow-up.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms capture examples, but varied language and conflicting accounts require synthesis beyond fixed fields.

steps.what: Record agreed follow-up questions, owners and dates.

tasks.design: A configured form in {WORKFLOW} collects examples alongside a structured signal pack from {CRM} and {ERP}. The buyer keeps the discovery conversation, then a bounded loop drafts a source-linked brief in {DOCS} from written notes and responses. Buyer approval releases the brief and creates explicitly agreed follow-up actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful knowledge was scattered across conversations and mailboxes. Fixed questionnaires captured requests but struggled to preserve context and contradictory accounts.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms remove repeated chasing and re-entry. Bounded drafting can organise written evidence while leaving discovery and interpretation with people.
tasks.still_hard: Colleague recollections are selective, vocal customers can dominate and unmet demand may leave no sales record. A polished summary can conceal weak evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Build enough trust for colleagues to share awkward examples and ask questions that uncover the need behind a requested product.

ambition.what: Include low-volume customer segments in the monthly assortment-needs review.

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends less time chasing replies and writing summaries, with more room to test weak signals through follow-up conversations. Assortment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate customer needs into supplier enquiries.
reach.learn: Learn to distinguish an underlying need from a preferred specification and preserve evidence gaps.

reach.task: Prioritise assortment experiments.
reach.learn: Learn evidence sampling, segment coverage and how to define a small commercial test.

evidence.claim: Configured forms and task routing can reduce feedback chasing and repeated entry.
A bounded model loop can draft themes from written feedback, with human checks for attribution and meaning.
Customer discovery still requires probing questions and judgement about whether examples represent broader demand.

assumptions: Step shares cover the whole interaction, including colleagues' response time.
The solution uses written notes and submitted examples; recording or transcription is outside the estimate.
Existing customer identifiers support aggregation without exposing unnecessary personal details.
GDPR governs customer and employee data; national rules determine consultation requirements. Employee scoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Where are customer requests already recorded, and which fields are reusable?
Which segments and colleagues are currently missing from feedback?
What access, retention and lawful-basis arrangements cover the proposed data reuse?
Are the agreed follow-up owners and dates consistently recorded in discussion notes?
research_questions: Which brief structure best preserves minority views and contradictory evidence?
How can the pilot detect themes supported only by repeated copies of the same customer example?
new_work: Review summaries against original examples and discussion notes.
Remove unnecessary personal details before processing.
Maintain category questions and feedback routing.
Check segment coverage and follow up on contradictory or weak signals.
tasks.statement: Obtain information about customer needs or preferences by conferring with sales or purchasing personnel.

tasks.short: Work with suppliers to source or develop products that meet commercial and quality requirements.

steps.what: Prepare product requirements from assortment gaps, customer needs and target costs.

loop.input: Approved assortment goals, customer feedback and quality requirements.
loop.output: A product brief with sourced requirements and explicit open questions.
loop.check: Use a fixed brief schema; verify target costs and required fields; buyer approves the brief.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported requirements remain blank for the buyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer feedback and assortment intentions need synthesis; fixed fields and calculations use templates.

steps.what: Send the brief and request proposals, samples and feasibility information.
Provide proposals, technical details and product samples.
Assess samples for quality, usability, presentation and fit with the assortment.
Discuss product changes, feasibility, price and delivery trade-offs with the supplier.
Confirm the revised specification and agreed acceptance conditions.

loop.input: Existing specification, buyer-written notes and agreed development changes.
loop.output: A revised specification with a source-linked change list.
loop.check: Buyer checks every changed requirement; unresolved quality questions go to the quality specialist.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; conflicting notes prevent approval and return to the buyer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiated changes arrive in free text; document versioning and unchanged fields remain deterministic.

steps.what: Track agreed sample revisions, tests and delivery milestones.

tasks.design: A product-development record in {PROJECT} links briefs, sample assessments and versioned specifications in {DOCS}. Bounded drafting prepares briefs and specification changes, while configured {WORKFLOW} routes approved requests through {EMAIL} and tracks milestones. Physical assessment and supplier discussions stay with the buyer and relevant specialists.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements and agreements are scattered across documents and conversations. Supplier development also depends on physical samples and trust, which software cannot settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates, version control and milestone workflows already exist. Bounded drafting can turn approved notes into consistent documents, and AI-assisted coding makes the connecting records easier to build.
tasks.still_hard: Samples may differ from production batches. Testing, intellectual property, safety requirements and supplier capability need specialist judgement and contractual clarity.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer notices product appeal and negotiates feasible compromises without weakening essential quality requirements.

ambition.what: A supplier product-development brief and sample-review service for small suppliers.

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends more time assessing samples and resolving design trade-offs, with less document chasing. Decision rights remain unchanged; formal product release still follows existing quality and commercial authority.

reach.task: Translate development agreements into supplier acceptance requirements.
reach.learn: Specification control, acceptance criteria and contractual remedies.

reach.task: Recommend which supplier development projects should receive funding.
reach.learn: Development portfolio assessment and supplier capability evaluation.

evidence.claim: Records, document versions and milestone reminders can support supplier product development deterministically.
Bounded drafting can prepare briefs and specification changes from approved sources, subject to human review.
The documented Australian report failure illustrates why generated document claims require source checks.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates; they exclude waiting for samples and laboratory tests.
Supplier contribution is shown to preserve the handoff; its effort is not counted as buyer time saved.
The people-and-judgement prior fits sample assessment and supplier discussion; preparation and paperwork can still change.
Buyer-written notes are sufficient; recording conversations is not required.
The buyer approves external requests and revised specifications; specialist release requirements remain separate.
GDPR applies to contact details. EU AI Act applicability and any consultation under national rules must be checked for the deployed use.
unknowns: Which products require specialist testing or formal release approval.
Who may approve specification changes and make supplier commitments.
Supplier access to shared records and restrictions on confidential designs.
Existing document templates, version controls and project workflows.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which document comparison methods reliably expose changed numeric product requirements?
Which standard product-development fields transfer well between supplier categories?
new_work: Review drafted requirements and specification changes.
Maintain brief templates and acceptance checklists.
Resolve conflicting notes and overdue supplier milestones.
Manage document permissions and supplier access.
tasks.statement: Collaborate with vendors to obtain or develop desired products.

tasks.short: Inspect merchandise and judge its quality, value and usable yield.

steps.what: Find the product specification, delivery details and inspection requirements.
Examine samples, test relevant properties and record defects.
Calculate defect rates, usable yield and adjusted merchandise value.
Decide whether to accept, hold or reject the merchandise.
Notify the supplier of defects and request the appropriate remedy.

tasks.design: A form in {WORKFLOW} assembles inspection requirements from {PROCUREMENT}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}, then captures the buyer's physical findings. Deterministic calculations produce yield and value estimates; the buyer authorises disposition in {OPS_SYSTEM} and approves a templated supplier notice through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inspection evidence was separated from order records, and product-specific calculations lived in individual workbooks. Physical examination could not be replaced by record automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, validation and formula engines are established technology. AI-assisted coding makes category-specific checklists and connections cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Sampling may miss defects. Texture, finish, durability and resale appeal can require physical expertise or specialist tests.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unexpected defects and judge whether a technically acceptable product meets customer expectations.

ambition.what: A supplier quality review combining recurring defects, usable yield and recovery outcomes.

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends less time finding specifications and calculating losses, leaving more time for difficult inspections and supplier remedies. Acceptance authority remains unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain inspection evidence against purchase orders.
reach.learn: Learn batch identifiers, specification versions and evidence needed for supplier credits.

reach.task: Review recurring supplier quality failures.
reach.learn: Learn sampling limitations and how defect costs affect supplier selection.

evidence.claim: Checklist generation, defect-rate calculations and templated supplier notices can be deterministic.
Physical inspection and acceptance decisions depend on merchandise properties, sampling and commercial judgement.

assumptions: Estimates cover one category with agreed inspection criteria and existing physical testing methods.
The scope excludes installing automated inspection equipment or developing a visual defect model.
Inspection findings are entered directly into the future form.
GDPR applies to identifiable people in inspection evidence; national rules determine consultation if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which categories require specialist testing or mandatory release procedures?
Who may release, hold or reject stock?
Are batch identifiers and specification versions reliable?
Can the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} support inspection forms and calculations through configuration?
research_questions: Which existing inspection features can replace custom development?
Which yield formulas and sampling methods are appropriate for the merchandise categories?
new_work: Maintain inspection criteria and specification versions.
Investigate missing measurements and implausible yield results.
Check that disposition updates reach the warehouse team.
Review supplier notices and track remedy outcomes.
tasks.statement: Inspect merchandise or products to determine quality, value, or yield.

tasks.short: Introduce new merchandise to sales staff through meetings and demonstrations.

steps.what: Collect approved product facts, prices, availability and supplier materials.
Prepare the merchandise presentation and likely questions.

loop.input: Approved product facts, permitted claims and audience description
loop.output: Presentation text and source-linked answers to likely questions
loop.check: Copy prices and specifications directly; buyer checks claims, relevance and unanswered questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per meeting; unsupported answers remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific explanations and likely questions require language beyond a fixed product template.

steps.what: Arrange the meeting, invite sales staff and organise samples.
Introduce merchandise, demonstrate samples and discuss selling situations.
Record questions, correct misunderstandings and assign follow-up owners.
Send the presentation, confirmed answers and follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Assemble current product facts from {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {DOCS}, then draft a source-linked presentation for buyer approval. Use {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW} for invitations and follow-up, with questions and owners recorded in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product information arrives in inconsistent formats, and meeting preparation is repeated for each launch. Questions and commitments often stay in personal notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations can reuse product records, and bounded drafting can turn approved facts into meeting materials. Scheduling and action tracking are existing software capabilities.
tasks.still_hard: Samples still need physical handling. Live demonstrations, objections and uncertain product claims need an informed person.
tasks.human_edge: The buyer connects product features to real selling situations and responds to hesitation or practical objections.

ambition.what: Recorded merchandise briefings with question follow-up for remote sales staff

tasks.altitude: The buyer spends less preparation time per launch and can include remote staff through reusable briefings. Product-claim and commercial commitment authority does not change.

reach.task: Obtain missing product specifications from suppliers
reach.learn: Specification checks, evidence for product claims and supplier escalation

evidence.claim: Shopify Sidekick generates product descriptions, supporting the narrower feasibility of merchandise text drafting.
Product-data assembly, scheduling and action tracking can use deterministic integrations and existing configuration.
Presentation quality, meeting effectiveness and build ranges remain unvalidated estimates for this setting.

assumptions: Meetings primarily introduce merchandise to internal sales staff.
Approved product facts and claims can be identified.
Samples are arranged by people; automation handles the checklist and requests.
Remote briefings use presentation and demonstration content without recording employee discussion.
unknowns: Whether meetings include external customers or distributors
Who approves product claims and audience access
Availability and reliability of product data interfaces
Recording permissions, retention rules and any consultation required under national rules
research_questions: Can the existing document templates produce usable presentations from structured product facts?
Which launch questions recur and can be answered from approved sources?
What briefing format works for remote sales staff?
new_work: Check generated claims and explanations before presentation.
Maintain product sources and audience-specific templates.
Resolve unanswered questions with named owners.
Refresh shared briefings when prices or availability change.
tasks.statement: Conduct sales meetings to introduce new merchandise.

role_batches.altitude: The buyer's week shifts from assembling evidence and maintaining workbooks toward negotiation, physical quality judgement and testing assortment choices. Commercial commitments, stock disposition and pricing approvals retain their existing decision rights unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Procurement clerks: connect approved supplier terms, inspection evidence and master-data quality.
Purchasing agents: turn customer evidence into precise supplier enquiries.
Purchasing managers: contribute better evidence to category margin, supplier risk and assortment decisions.
skills_to_grow: Supplier and product identifiers, effective dates and data reconciliation.
Checking extracted clauses and source-linked summaries.
Configuring forms, approval limits and exception routing.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a regular category decision service that connects supplier concessions, quality losses, ageing stock and underserved customer needs, with a named commercial owner approving each consequential action.

role_batches.altitude: The buyer's week shifts toward assortment decisions, sample assessment, supplier discussions and store trade-offs. Better evidence supports recommendations; spending, product-release and budget rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Purchasing manager: prepare category and cross-store budget recommendations.
Purchasing agent: turn commercial decisions into clear supplier acceptance requirements.
Procurement clerk: improve order, return and credit exception handling.
skills_to_grow: Data quality, unit conversions and approval controls.
Source checking for extracted terms and drafted specifications.
Facilitation of store and supplier trade-offs.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a merchandise improvement service that combines frequent assortment reallocations, small-supplier development support and store-specific buying reviews. Begin with existing approval rights and seek explicit delegation for any expanded trial budget.

role_batches.altitude: The buyer's week shifts toward assortment judgement, supplier challenge and inventory scenarios. Preparation becomes faster, while purchasing commitments and environmental exceptions remain subject to explicit delegated authority.
reach: Support purchasing managers with category inventory and supplier-risk scenarios.
Help purchasing agents request comparable supplier evidence.
Help procurement clerks resolve order and label-data exceptions.
skills_to_grow: Commercial scenario analysis and exception judgement
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a shared category decision service that combines demand scenarios, supplier comparisons and environmental evidence for buyers with limited analytical support.

role_batches.altitude: The buyer's week shifts toward merchandise judgement, supplier questions and staff coaching, with less report assembly and meeting administration. Existing approval rights remain; better evidence supports more frequent commercial proposals.
reach: Purchasing manager: category budget allocation and competitive response decisions
Purchasing agent: supplier specification checks and evidence gathering
Procurement clerk: reliable merchandise records and routine order correction
skills_to_grow: Promotion economics and cautious interpretation of historical results
Data quality checks and exception handling
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a weekly category review that connects competitor offers, stock availability, proposed promotions and sales-team questions into timely buying recommendations.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
